name: Noah
title: Builder of the Ark
summary: Noah was a righteous man who lived at a time when human wickedness was great on the earth. God commanded him to build an ark to save his family and the animals from the great flood. He is an important example of faith and obedience in the Bible.

keyEvents.title: Noah Finds Favor with God
keyEvents.description: In a time when all human wickedness was great, Noah found favor in the eyes of the Lord because he was a righteous and blameless man.

keyEvents.title: God Commands Noah to Build the Ark
keyEvents.description: God gave Noah detailed instructions to build a large ark of cypress wood to save his family and all animal species from the coming flood.

keyEvents.title: The Great Flood
keyEvents.description: Noah, his family, and the animals entered the ark, and God sent a flood that covered the whole earth for forty days and forty nights.

keyEvents.title: The Ark Lands on Ararat
keyEvents.description: After the waters receded, the ark landed in the mountains of Ararat. Noah sent out a dove which eventually did not return, showing that the ground was dry again.

keyEvents.title: God's Covenant with Noah and the Rainbow
keyEvents.description: After the flood, Noah built an altar and offered sacrifices to the Lord. God established a covenant with Noah and set the rainbow as a sign that he would never again destroy the earth with a flood.

keyEvents.title: Noah as a Model of Faith in the New Testament
keyEvents.description: In Hebrews, Noah is highlighted as an example of faith. By faith he built the ark in reverence, and he became an heir to the righteousness that comes by faith. Peter also refers to him as a preacher of righteousness.
